subject: Annotated attack surface mapping and threat-summary (RFI)
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@octavia.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: DevSecOps Team <security@octavia.com>
Date: 2027-06-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood RFI: annotated attack surface and threat summary

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking our RFI. As part of Octavia's procurement for a hosted inference platform, we need an annotated network/architecture deliverable that shows your isolation model end-to-end. Specifically could you provide:

- A single-page annotated diagram showing tenant boundaries (shared vs dedicated), service-to-service zones, KV-cache placement and lifecycle, ingress/e egress control points, bastion/management access, and expected failover paths.
- A 1-2 page threat-model summary that lists plausible attack paths (privilege escalation, lateral movement via shared caches, exfiltration via egress) and the high-level mitigations you apply.
- Confirmation whether per-tenant request IDs and tracing are available for forensic purposes, and how long request/audit logs are retained by default.

Timeline: can you send initial artifacts by EOD 2027-06-10? We may need to schedule a short follow-up call to walk the diagram.

We can execute an NDA if you prefer us not to publish the diagram internally.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Senior Security Architect
Octavia Systems

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@octavia.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-06T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood RFI: annotated attack surface and threat summary

Hi Liam,

Appreciate the clear ask — we'll put together an annotated diagram and a concise threat-summary that maps directly to the items you listed. I'm looping in Rishi (security lead, infra) and Marissa (product infra) to assemble the artifacts.

Proposed next steps:
- We'll share a PDF annotated diagram + a threat-model doc by 2027-06-07 morning PT.
- If helpful, let's do a 20–30 minute walkthrough; I'm free 2027-06-08 10:00–10:30 PT. Does that work for your team?

We generally can provide per-tenant request IDs and retain audit logs for 90 days by default; Rishi will confirm retention windows and logging endpoints. If you want the diagram under NDA we can accept that — we'll provide a quick NDA link if needed.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Product Security
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@octavia.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: DevSecOps Team <security@octavia.com>
Date: 2027-06-06T12:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood RFI: annotated attack surface and threat summary

Thanks Kimberly — 10:00 PT on the 8th works for us.

A couple of clarifying points for the diagram so we can review effectively:
- Please indicate cloud-provider egress NAT/whitelist expectations per path (i.e., which outbound flows need customer-managed allowlists versus Redwood-managed egress).
- Show whether KV cache persistence is per-tenant (isolated) or shared across tenants and where (if anywhere) it's persisted to durable storage.
- If you publish request IDs/tracing, can you indicate sample headers/fields we should expect in logs for correlation.

We'll sign an NDA before you send the PDF if that simplifies internal handling.

Cheers,
Liam

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@octavia.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-07T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood RFI: annotated attack surface and threat summary

Hi Liam — attaching the items requested. Per our earlier exchange (On Sun, Jun 6, 2027, Liam wrote: "Please indicate cloud-provider egress NAT/whitelist expectations..."), see the highlights below.

Attachments (stubs):
- redwood-annotated-attack-surface.pdf (single-page, labeled zones, arrows for trust-boundaries, egress points)
- redwood-threat-model-summary.docx (2 pages, prioritized attack paths and mitigations)
- network-segmentation-v1.vsdx (working Visio, no PII)

Key clarifications (short):
- Egress & allowlists: Redwood-managed outbound to public model repositories and telemetry endpoints uses shared egress pools in hosted mode; customers can opt for customer-managed NAT or VPC peering in Dedicated/Private deployments. The PDF annotates which external endpoints customers must whitelist when using customer egress.
- KV cache persistence: By default KV cache is in-memory and scoped per model instance; in Hosted shared tenancy the cache is ephemeral and not durable to multi-tenant persistent storage. For Dedicated/Private we offer isolated cache instances that can be configured to persist to customer-attached volumes — this is shown and labeled in the diagram.
- Tracing & request IDs: We emit a per-request trace id in header X-RW-Trace-Id and include it in audit logs. Default audit retention is 90 days; longer retention and S3 export can be configured under enterprise contracts (we documented export hooks in the attached doc).

Relevant links: hubspot deal record https://hubspot.com/deal/OCTV-2027-013 and internal write-up: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Annotated+Attack+Surface+Mapping

If you'd like, we can walk the PDF during the 2027-06-08 10:00 PT slot and mark any sensitive elements that should remain covered under NDA.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Security Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-annotated-attack-surface.pdf (application/pdf), redwood-threat-model-summary.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document), network-segmentation-v1.vsdx (application/vnd.visio)
